title: noah-chen-sre-oncall-scratchpad-2026-03-06
content:
On-call scratchpad - Noah Chen (2026-03-06)

Summary:
- Single-page shift (overnight). Primary noise: paging storm for increased 5xx rate hitting hosted-api /v1/generate route (region: us-west-2). PD incident: SRE-4567.

Timeline (local times PST):
- 02:12 AM - PagerDuty alert: hosted-api-5xx-rate-high (threshold: 5% over 5m). Alert group: hosted-api-prod-usw2.
- 02:15 AM - First ack (me). Checked Grafana (hosted-api /v1/generate p50/p95 latency and 5xx rate). 5xx jumped to ~12% and error spikes correlate with model "rwd-xl-13b" rollout.
- 02:20 AM - Noticed a deployment of rwd-xl-13b on dedicated pool (canary) completed ~02:05; traffic split policy may have mis-routed more traffic than expected. Slack: #prod-ops shows deployment by infra-automation.
- 02:22 AM - Scoped to node pool: nodes g4dn.* with kernel version mismatch showing repeated OOM-kill in pod logs.
- 02:28 AM - Mitigation: Updated routing to fallback to rwd-xl-13b-v1 (previous stable) via routing policy change (Console -> rollouts -> revert canary traffic to 0%).
- 02:35 AM - Error rate dropped to ~1.8%. Continued monitoring.
- 03:10 AM - Follow-up: restarted two pods in pool serving rwd-xl-13b (kubectl rollout restart deployment/hosted-api-rwd-xl-13b -n hosted-prod). No further 5xx spikes.

Quick commands used:
- kubectl -n hosted-prod get pods -o wide | grep rwd-xl-13b
- kubectl logs deployment/hosted-api -c model-runner --since=10m | grep "OOMKilled"
- curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health (from bastion)

Root cause (initial hypothesis):
- Canaries were shifted to a node pool with a slightly different kernel/runtime (recent kernel patch on g4dn AMI). Some model runners hit an edge case leading to memory blowups under certain sequence-length distributions. Combined with the traffic split config mistake, too many requests hit the affected pods causing a visible increase in 5xx.

Immediate actions taken:
- Rolled back traffic from canary (routing policy revert).
- Restarted affected pods and cordoned one problematic host for further investigation.
- Added temporary alert suppression for noisy downstream infra alert (to avoid paging loop) - will review suppression window and owner.

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- (High) Create SRE ticket with full timeline, attach logs and Grafana panels -> SRE-4567 (already created)
- (High) Coordinate with infra-release team to audit AMI/kernel differences and recent patches applied to g4dn pools. Owner: Ethan Park. Due: 2026-03-09.
- (Medium) Update runbook section "hosted-api model rollout" with clearer preflight checks (node compatibility + memory profile smoke test). Owner: me. ETA: 2026-03-10.
- (Medium) Add automated canary traffic limit (hard cap) to prevent >10% traffic to unverified canaries. Owner: infra-release. Ticket: INFRA-782.
- (Low) Add additional telemetry for per-model memory usage (sampled). Owner: observability team (Rachel Lee).

Notes to self (scratchy):
- Remember to include pod-level oom logs, kernel messages, and node AMI id in postmortem.
- Check if there was any corresponding autoscaler flurry -> might have caused pod churn.
- Check Console rollouts audit logs for who changed the split -> link: https://console.redwood.com/rollouts/logs/rollback/1234 (add to ticket)

Runbook TODOs (quick list):
- Add step: "If 5xx > 5% after canary deploy -> immediately set canary traffic to 0% and tag release as hold."
- Add runbook command snippets for safe rollback and traffic reweighting (include CLI and Console instructions).
- Add contact list for infra-release + model-owner + oncall SRE.

Post-incident meeting: create invite for 2026-03-08 10:00am PST (30m) with infra-release, model owners, obs, and oncall. Agenda: root cause confirm, rollout gating improvements, automation. Owner: Mia Li.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did kernel patch hit only g4dn pool? Is there a staggered AMI rollout upstream?
- Was there any spike in long-sequence requests that could have triggered higher memory usage? (check request distribution for last 6h)

Other minor items handled this shift:
- Cleared alert storm for dns-flap-01 (suppressed, follow-up ticket created INFRA-789).
- Reminder: update personal oncall notes template to include "mitigation commands" section for faster handoffs.

End of notes.

-- Noah
